facts.text: Simpsonville earned its name in 1850 when Charles Simpson, the first postmaster, gave the community its modern identity.
The historic Simpsonville Mill, a water‑powered grist and saw mill, once stood beside the Middle Patuxent River, powering local grain and lumber production.
Before settlers arrived, the Susquehannock and Piscataway tribes used the Middle Patuxent Valley for hunting and gathering, leaving behind prehistoric stone tools.
Archaeologists uncovered over 42,000 artifacts—including millstones and early Native American lithics—showing Simpsonville’s long industrial and cultural history.
Today, remnants of the mill site lie partially under modern roads near Columbia, preserving the story of a once‑thriving rural milling hub.
